sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A bike rental costs $5 plus $3 per hour. The total cost was $20. Which equation represents the number of hours, x?

steps: The flat fee of 5 is added once.
The hourly rate of 3 multiplies the hours, x.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A bike rental costs $3 plus $11 per hour. If the total cost was $113, how many hours, x, were rented?
A student solves 5x - 4 = 31. They write 5x = 35, then say x = 35. Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The student forgot to divide both sides by 5; the correct solution is x = 7.
The student should have multiplied by 5 instead of dividing; x = 175.
The student subtracted incorrectly; the correct solution is x = 27/5.

items.prompt: A student says 2x - 18 = 2x - 18 has one solution because they can solve for x. Which statement correctly analyzes the equation?
choices: The equation has infinitely many solutions; both sides are identical for every x.
The equation has no solution; simplifying gives -18 = -18, which is never true.
The equation cannot be classified without graphing it.
The equation has exactly one solution, found by dividing both sides by the coefficient of x.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.
